After restricting the analysis to non-overlapping Korean NHIS cohorts, the direction and significance of benefit are preserved (HR 0.85; P=0.023). These data isolate the pharmacologic contribution from ablation in the EAST-AFNET 4 framework and confirm that drug-first rhythm control carries independent prognostic value. The two-study evidence base limits definitive conclusions and reinforces the case for a dedicated non-Korean external replication dataset.
n6373a2e5ebc8: Background: Constipation is common among patients with heart failure (HF) and has been associated with increased readmission risk. Polyethylene glycol (PEG), lactulose, and stimulant laxatives are widely used in this population, yet their comparative cardiovascular safety is poorly characterized. Methods: We conducted a new user, active comparator, propensity score matched (PSM) retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (66 U.S. healthcare organizations). Adults with HF and constipation diagnosed within one year of the HF diagnosis between 2021 and 2026 were included. Patients with liver diseases (cirrhosis, hepatic encephalopathy, hepatic failure, portal hypertension) were excluded. A 6-month laxative free washout preceded initiation of the index laxative. Three independent 1:1 PSM comparisons: PEG vs contact laxatives (senna, bisacodyl; n=10,174), PEG vs lactulose (n=3,860), and contact laxatives vs lactulose (n=4,601), were conducted, ensuring balanced demographics, comorbidities, prior electrolyte disorders, and cardiovascular medications, including diuretics. Outcomes were assessed at 30 and 90 days. All post-match standardized mean differences were <0.04. Results: Compared with stimulant laxatives, PEG was associated with lower 30-day modified 3-point MACE (Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events: cerebral infarction, myocardial infarction, or all-cause mortality) (11.1% vs 13.5%; RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.77-0.89; p<.001), lower mortality (3.9% vs 4.9%; RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.70-0.90; p<.001), and fewer arrhythmias (28.3% vs 29.8%, RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.91-0.99; p=.012). At 90 days, PEG remained associated with lower modified MACE (16.6% vs 18.7%; RR 0.89; p<.001) and mortality (6.7% vs 7.9%; RR 0.85; p<.001). However, hospitalization, acute kidney injury (AKI), and electrolyte imbalance did not differ significantly. Lactulose was associated with lower rates of 30-day MACE, hospitalization, and mortality compared with both PEG and contact laxatives. Conclusions: In this large propensity matched new user cohort of patients with HF and constipation, PEG was associated with lower short term mortality than stimulant laxatives, without excess risk of hospitalization, AKI, or electrolyte imbalance. Lactulose showed no excess cardiovascular risk, although residual confounding remained. These findings support prospective evaluation of non-stimulant laxatives as potentially safer constipation treatment strategies in HF.
n42b4b946710d: Background: Fractional flow reserve derived from computed tomography angiography (FFR-CT) is a promising tool to non-invasively assess the hemodynamic severity of coronary lesions. However, real-world uptake and accessibility in the US are not well-characterized Research Question: How often is FFR-CT performed in the US, where is it performed, and how accessible is it? Methods: Using 2024 data from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Part B datasets, we quantified, as a proportion of computed tomography coronary angiography (CTCA), the adoption of FFR-CT as well as provider-level and state-level variability in FFR-CT adoption. Additionally, we assessed geographical proximity to centers with FFR-CT capabilities in the US. CTCA was identified using Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) code 75574 and FFR-CT was identified using CPT code 75580. Data on the provider-level utilization of FFR-CT as a percentage of CTA was limited to providers with ≥11 CTCA and CT-FFRs. Results: From 210,289 CTCAs performed in the US in 2024 for Medicare beneficiaries, a total of 29,270 FFR-CT procedures were performed (13.9%). Out of 7,480 providers reading CTCA, 2,421 (32.4%) performed FFR-CT. Provider-level FFR-CT adoption as a % of CTCA varied widely (IQR among providers performing ≥11 CTCA and CT-FFRs: 19.7% to 44.9%), with 18.3% using FFR-CT in >50% of CTA reads. States with the highest adoption of FFR-CT (as % of CTA) included West Virginia (428 FFR-CT out of 1,211 CTCA; 35.3%), Delaware (199 FFR-CT out of 653 CTCA; 30.5%), and North Carolina (1,559 FFR-CT out of 6,082 CTCAs). The weighted-median distance to the nearest FFR-CT-capable facility (with ≥11 FFR-CT procedures in 2024) was 23.3km, with 52.7 million persons in the US (16%) living >100km away from the nearest facility. Conclusion: Nationwide adoption of FFR-CT shows considerable provider-level and state-level heterogeneity, with one-third of those performing CTCA additionally performing FFR. Large swathes of the US have minimal access to FFR-CT-capable facilities.
n520ac4fdf833: Background: Although clinically validated risk scores exist, accurately predicting acute heart failure (HF) exacerbation and the transition to HF with recovered ejection fraction (HFrecEF) remains challenging. Recently, the continuous monitoring of wearable-derived daily biometrics has demonstrated promising prognostic utility. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that outcome-specific digital performance indices derived from wearable data could effectively predict both HF exacerbation and HFrecEF. Methods: We prospectively enrolled 363 patients with HF from the Hokuriku-plus HF Registry equipped with a wearable device (Fitbit® Inspire 3). Wearable-derived biometric features collected over a 1-week period prior to hospital discharge were extracted. Using multi-output partial least squares regression, these features were dimensionally reduced into six distinct axes, collectively termed the “7-day performance chart”. From this chart, a 1-dimensional“7- day performance index (PI)” was newly calculated for each specific outcome: 7-day PI HFE for HF exacerbation and 7-day PI HFrecEF for HFrecEF (defined as baseline left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF]<40%, a >10% absolute increase, and a 6-month LVEF>40%). We assessed the predictive values of these absolute index values at 6 months. Results: Among the participants, 34 patients (58% male, mean age, 63.6 ± 12.2 years; history of HF, 29.4%; mean NT-proBNP, 1863.4 ± 3745.5 pg/mL; and mean LVEF, 32.1 ± 12.7%) were analyzed for HF exacerbation outcome, and 30 patients (88%) with HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) were analyzed for HFrecEF outcome. The 7-day performance chart accounted for 68.1% of the variance in these multidimensional wearable features. The 7-day PI HFE was significantly higher in the HF exacerbation group than in the non-exacerbation group (0.628 vs. -0.193, P< 0.01) with an AUC of 0.889 (95%CI: 0.773-1.000). Similarly, the 7-day PI HFrecEF was significantly lower in the HFrecEF group than in the non-recovered EF group (-0.913 vs. 0.398, P< 0.001) with an AUC of 0.971 (95%CI: 0.913-1.000). (Figure). Conclusions: These outcome-specific 7-day PIs represented novel composite digital biomarkers that effectively predict both HF exacerbation and HFrecEF. Integrating these tools into routine HF management could enable earlier clinical interventions and improve long-term outcomes.
n752878c7ba63: Background: Randomized trials of tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) have consistently shown improvements in tricuspid regurgitation severity, symptoms, and health status, whereas early analyses of death or first heart-failure hospitalization (HFH) have shown limited clinical-event separation. Severe tricuspid regurgitation represents a chronic right-sided heart-failure phenotype, therefore treatment effects may emerge over longer follow-up period. Objectives: To evaluate whether T-TEER may reduce longer-term recurrent HFH burden and to quantify the probability of clinically meaningful benefit using Bayesian sparse-trial synthesis. Methods: We performed an aggregate-data meta-analysis of randomized T-TEER trials reporting longer-term recurrent HFH outcomes. The primary estimate was the treatment-to-control recurrent HFH effect ratio, synthesizing randomized trial-reported recurrent-event rate ratios or hazard ratios on the log scale. Random-effects synthesis incorporated a skeptical Bayesian normal prior centered at no effect [log(RR)=0, SD=0.35]. Absolute recurrent-HFH reductions were calculated per 100 patient-years and used to estimate the number of patients requiring treatment over 2 years to prevent one HFH event. Given that post-1-year crossover may attenuate intention-to-treat estimates, a prespecified mixture-based crossover-contamination sensitivity analysis was applied. Results: Two randomized T-TEER datasets contributed longer-term recurrent-HFH evidence. TRILUMINATE Pivotal reported recurrent HFH rates of 0.19 versus 0.26 events/patient-year with T-TEER + OMT versus OMT (optimal medical therapy), corresponding to a joint frailty hazard ratio of 0.72. TRI.FR extended follow-up, with no crossover and prespecified recurrent-event analysis, reported 37 versus 64 total HFH events for T-TEER + OMT versus OMT, with a rate ratio of 0.52. The pooled recurrent-HFH effect favored T-TEER (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.48-0.87). The mean absolute reduction was 7.1 fewer HFH events per 100 patient-years, corresponding to approximately 7 patients requiring T-TEER + OMT rather than OMT alone over 2 years to prevent one HFH event. Bayesian analysis yielded a posterior median RR of 0.69, 95% credible interval 0.53-0.91, with posterior probabilities of 99.5% for any benefit, 84.7% for at least 20% reduction, and 52.9% for at least 30% reduction. Crossover-contamination sensitivity shifted the TRILUMINATE recurrent-HFH RR from 0.73 toward approximately 0.66 under plausible assumptions. Conclusions: Longer randomized follow-up suggests that the clinical benefit of T-TEER emerges over time and is recurrent-event based, as shown by reduced HFH burden rather than early separation in mortality or first-event endpoints. Recurrent HFH burden and crossover-aware estimates should be prioritized in future tricuspid intervention trials.
nc9a1b4d5fa9d: Introduction: The colon may be where Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) begins—but not where its consequences end. Across heart failure, cardiac surgery, and other cardiovascular populations, CDI has been linked to death, stroke, renal failure, and substantial healthcare burden. Yet the full extent of its cardiovascular footprint remains undefined. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to determine whether CDI represents more than a gastrointestinal disease in cardiovascular medicine. Methods Following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261416645 ), PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were systematically searched from inception through May 2026 for observational studies evaluating the impact of Clostridioides difficile infection in cardiovascular populations. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Outcomes of interest included mortality, cardiovascular and cardiorenal complications, healthcare utilization, and CDI incidence. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed in R (version 4.5.0) to generate pooled effect estimates with 95% confidence intervals. Results: Thirteen studies comprising 4.38 million patients were included in qualitative synthesis, of which 12 studies were eligible for meta-analysis. CDI was associated with significantly higher in-hospital mortality (RR 2.45, 95% CI 1.70-3.53; P<0.001) , cardiac arrest ( OR 2.74, 95% CI 1.58-4.74; P<0.01) , and AKI/renal failure/new dialysis ( RR 2.77, 95% CI 2.26-3.39; P<0.001 ). Patients with CDI incurred $135,205 higher hospitalization costs ( 95% CI $23,419-$246,990; P=0.018) , with CDI affecting approximately 1 in 100 cardiovascular patients (pooled incidence 1.07%, 95% CI 0.55-2.08). Qualitative synthesis further linked CDI to stroke, prolonged hospitalization, mechanical ventilation, reduced long-term survival, and greater healthcare utilization. Overall, CDI was associated with a 2.5-fold increase in mortality and a nearly 3-fold increase in major cardiorenal complications , suggesting consequences that extend well beyond the gastrointestinal tract. Conclusions: Clostridioides difficile infection may represent one of the most underrecognized risk states in cardiovascular medicine. Far from being a purely gastrointestinal disease, CDI was consistently associated with worse survival, greater clinical complexity, and escalating healthcare burden across diverse cardiac populations. Our findings suggest that the cardiovascular footprint of CDI has been hiding in plain sight. When the gut fails, the heart may pay a far greater price than previously recognized.
nc3a410080c44: Background: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is a revascularization strategy for patients with high-risk spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD), particularly those with left main or multivessel SCAD; failed percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI); or hemodynamic instability. However, contemporary data on early procedural outcomes, graft patency, and long-term clinical outcomes remain limited. Methods: We performed a retrospective analysis of Mayo Clinic SCAD Registry patients who underwent CABG for acute SCAD between 1996 and 2020. Baseline clinical presentation, angiographic characteristics, procedural details, graft characteristics, and outcomes were analyzed. Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed to assess major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) defined as death, recurrent SCAD, myocardial infarction (MI), stroke/transient ischemic attack, or repeat revascularization. Results: This cohort included 72 patients treated with CABG for acute SCAD. Mean age was 42±9 years, and 97% were women. Upon presentation, 68% had STEMI, 31% had NSTEMI; and 26% had cardiac arrest/ventricular arrhythmia. Left main SCAD was present in 35%, and multivessel SCAD in 46%. CABG was emergent in 99% and performed after failed PCI in 40%. Mechanical circulatory support was required in 54%. A total of 142/143 grafts were successfully performed as planned. Left internal mammary artery grafts were used in 53 patients (76%), and saphenous vein grafts were used in 54 patients (76%), while radial artery and right internal mammary artery grafts were infrequent (1.4% each). On-pump CABG was performed in 74%. Mean cardiopulmonary bypass time and mean aortic cross-clamp time were 75±37 and 56±21 minutes, respectively. Thirty-day postoperative complications occurred in 40%, including bleeding requiring re-exploration, cardiogenic shock, respiratory failure, ventricular arrhythmias, and severe left ventricular dysfunction. Angiography after CABG in 21 (29%) patients showed with graft occlusion in 9/21 (42.9%) at median time of 4 years (IQR 2.4-7.3). Causes of graft failure included competitive native LAD flow after vessel healing (most frequent in 88%), thrombotic occlusion, and graft obstruction. The estimated 5-year MACE rate was 32%. Conclusions: CABG remains an important revascularization strategy for high-risk SCAD, achieving high procedural success, but also high risk of early complications. Long-term graft patency is limited, and patients have a notable risk of future MACE. These findings provide one of the largest contemporary assessments of CABG outcomes in SCAD and support the need for careful surveillance following surgical revascularization.
nd71af20f52f6: Introduction: Cardiac amyloidosis causes progressive myocardial infiltration and carries a poor prognosis, yet risk stratification when ejection fraction is preserved remains difficult. Because left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is often preserved until advanced disease and may underestimate myocardial dysfunction, strain imaging may improve risk stratification. Research Question: We evaluated whether cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived myocardial strain is independently associated with all-cause mortality among patients with cardiac amyloidosis and preserved LVEF. Methods: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study at a tertiary hospital using a CMR database spanning 2008-2023. Eligible patients met established diagnostic criteria for cardiac amyloidosis, including histologic confirmation by endomyocardial biopsy, extracardiac biopsy with characteristic CMR findings of cardiac involvement, or grade 2-3 technetium-99m pyrophosphate uptake in the absence of monoclonal gammopathy. Amyloid subtypes were classified as light-chain amyloidosis (AL) or transthyretin amyloidosis (TTR) based on histopathology and nuclear imaging. Studies with poor image quality were excluded. Left ventricular (LV) and right ventricular (RV) global longitudinal strain were quantified with feature-tracking dedicated software. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality from the date of CMR. The primary predictors were LVEF and CMR-derived LV and RV longitudinal strain. Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, and amyloid subtype estimated hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Strain analyses were prespecified in patients with preserved LVEF. Results: Among 184 patients (92 TTR, 92 AL; mean age 82±9 vs 67±10 years; 85% vs 53% male), TTR patients had greater wall thickness, ventricular volumes, and late gadolinium enhancement burden. Over 24 months, mortality was higher in AL than TTR (33.7% vs 14.1%, p=0.002, Figure 1). Each 1% increase in LVEF was associated with lower mortality (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-1.00, p=0.034). Among 116 patients with preserved LVEF, each 1% increase in absolute LV longitudinal strain was associated with 23% lower mortality (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.61-0.97, p=0.029), and each 1% increase in absolute RV longitudinal strain with 11% lower mortality (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.80-0.99, p=0.035), independent of age, sex, and subtype (Figure 2). Conclusion: In cardiac amyloidosis, CMR-derived LV and RV longitudinal strain were independently associated with all-cause mortality among patients with preserved LVEF, supporting strain as an early marker of adverse prognosis.
n6c3c21e7ecf3: Background: Myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery (MINS) is a common, often clinically silent perioperative complication associated with mortality. Although ECG foundation models have emerged, they were developed mainly from diagnostic 12-lead ECGs, leaving their applicability to continuous intraoperative single-lead monitoring unclear. Whether such embeddings improve MINS prediction beyond clinical variables, and whether full-surgery modeling outperforms brief ECG snapshots, remains unknown. Methods: We retrospectively studied adults undergoing intra-abdominal or intrathoracic non-cardiac surgery under general anesthesia lasting >1 h at a tertiary center from 2016 to 2021. The primary outcome was MINS, defined as postoperative cardiac troponin elevation within 3 days. Intraoperative lead-II ECG was encoded with a 1-lead variant of ECGFounder, producing a 1,024-dimensional embedding for each 10-second segment. We compared snapshot embeddings from early and late 10-minute surgical windows modeled by linear probe, and full-surgery embeddings modeled by a bidirectional Simplified State-Space (S5) sequence model. Each strategy was fused with 16 clinical variables spanning demographics, preoperative laboratory values, ASA classification, surgical context, comorbidities, and intraoperative transfusion. Models were evaluated using patient-level 5-fold cross-validation. Pairwise differences in AUROC and AUPRC were estimated using paired bootstrap with 2,000 replicates. Calibration was assessed using Brier score, calibration intercept and slope, and expected calibration error (ECE). Results: Among 2,966 surgical cases (2,807 patients), 14.7% developed MINS. Adding intraoperative ECG embeddings to clinical variables improved prediction compared with clinical variables alone. The full-surgery S5 plus clinical model achieved an AUROC of 0.778 (95% CI, 0.754-0.802) and an AUPRC of 0.448 (95% CI, 0.405-0.492), compared with 0.758 and 0.367 for the clinical-only model (∆ AUROC, +0.020; p=0.049; ∆ AUPRC, +0.081; p<0.001). The snapshot plus clinical model showed similar discrimination to the S5 plus clinical model, with an AUROC of 0.778 and an AUPRC of 0.432 (versus S5: ∆ AUROC 0.000; ∆ AUPRC, +0.016; both not significant). Calibration was better with the snapshot plus clinical model than with the S5 plus clinical model, with lower Brier score (0.104 vs. 0.128), calibration slope closer to 1 (0.92 vs. 1.89), and lower ECE (0.017 vs. 0.146). Conclusions: Intraoperative ECG foundation-model embeddings fused with clinical variables significantly improved MINS prediction over clinical variables alone. Full-surgery temporal modeling did not outperform snapshot embeddings from early and late operative windows, suggesting that change between induction and emergence ECG captures the prognostic signal.
n252c9afc2125: Background: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (HCM) is diagnosed by unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) ≥15mm. This threshold is unadjusted for age and sex, contributing to diagnostic uncertainty for unexplained hypertrophy in the sub-diagnostic ‘gray-zone’ (≥12 to <15 mm). We characterized the genetic architecture of gray-zone LVH and compared clinical features and outcomes between carriers and non-carriers of rare variants in HCM-associated or HCM-genocopy genes. Methods: The Royal Brompton (RBH) Biobank prospectively enrolled 6,548 patients referred for diagnostic Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR) imaging. Subjects with gray-zone LV maximum wall thickness (LVMWT ≥12 <15mm) were included, excluding those aged <16 years, with >mild aortic stenosis, a confirmed HCM phenocopy (e.g. infiltrative or syndromic LVH), a known family history of HCM, or isolated apical hypertrophy (where alternative criteria apply). Patients underwent genetic sequencing, and were assessed for rare (protein altering, allele frequency < 1 in 1000) variants in 28 genes with strong/definitive evidence for HCM or other genetic causes of LVH. Results: In total, 270 patients with gray-zone LVH were identified (mean age 58.3±13.9 years; male 79.6%; European ancestry 83.7%; LVMWT 12.9±0.8mm; hypertensive 53.0%; diabetic 13.3%), of whom 230 underwent genetic analysis. Over a median follow-up of 11.37 years [IQR 10.19-12.73] there were 44 deaths. Patients were most commonly referred for evaluation of possible cardiomyopathy (n=133, 57.8%), ischemia (n=32, 13.9%) or ventricular dysfunction (n=28, 12.2%). n11c212fbfe09: and Introduction: Eosinophilic myocarditis (EM) is a rare cause of acute heart failure. The focal nature of cell infiltrates on endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) can lead to misdiagnosis. Heart rate was in the 150s with O2 saturation 90% on HFNC. POCUS showed a severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, confirmed at 20-25% on TTE. Troponin was 6,780 ng/L, BNP 2,500 pg/mL, WBC 16х10 9 /L with 15% eosinophils, and CRP 84 mg/L. Chest x-ray showed bilateral infiltrates. EMB showed sparse lymphocytic infiltrate with interstitial fibrosis, suggestive of a resolving myocarditis. She was treated for CAP and diuresed. She required intubation as her respiratory status worsened. Bronchoscopy with BAL revealed 75% eosinophils, and peripheral eosinophils rose to 50% by day 10. Re-examination of the EMB slides was requested, revealing eosinophilic infiltration consistent with EM (Image 1). Workup including ANCA, BCR-ABL, flow cytometry, and stool Strongyloides was negative. Final diagnosis was idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome with EM. Therapeutic Interventions: Pulse-dose methylprednisolone 1g IV daily for three days was initiated on day 10, followed by 80mg IV daily for two weeks, then a prednisone taper. Eosinophils dropped to 2% within 48 hours of pulse-dose steroids. GDMT was started as tolerated. Follow-up & Outcomes: Serial TTEs showed persistently reduced LVEF at 25%. She discharged to inpatient rehab on day 34 and completed a month of rehab with cardiology, rheumatology, and hematology follow-up arranged. Discussion: This case demonstrated that early EMB results can misclassify EM as resolving myocarditis, which delayed treatment. The pivot point was a BAL finding of 75% eosinophils, prompting a re-review of biopsy slides that revealed eosinophilic infiltrates not seen initially. Rapid response to steroids confirmed the diagnosis. The persistently reduced LVEF is likely from myocardial injury, highlighting the consequences of this diagnostic pitfall. n66f6927a2155: Background Patients with hypoplastic ventricles may undergo initial single-ventricle (SV) palliation, and subsequently either continue along a SV pathway or undergo conversion to a biventricular (BiV) circulation. We describe early outcomes after BiV repair and risk factors for prolonged duration of mechanical ventilation (DOMV). Methods Using an institutional database from a high-volume BiV center, we reviewed patients with single ventricle physiology or anatomy precluding standard neonatal BiV repair who underwent BiV conversion between 3/1/2007-9/30/2024. Anatomic categories included unbalanced AV canal (AVC), congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (ccTGA), double outlet right ventricle (DORV), DORV-AVC, hypoplastic left heart (HLH), and others. Prior palliations included stage 1 Norwood, hybrid palliation/PDA stent, bidirectional Glenn (BDG), Fontan, and pulmonary artery band (PAB). Bivariate and multivariate Cox regression evaluated time to extubation with Fine-Gray models to account for death as a competing risk. Two exposure models were examined: (1) anatomic or palliation category (ccTGA or PAB as each reference) and (2) anatomy-palliation combinations (ccTGA + PAB as the reference). Models were adjusted for bypass time and postoperative maximum vasoactive inotropic score (VIS), junctional ectopic tachycardia (JET), and renal dysfunction. Extubation rates and rate ratios are presented with lower values indicative of worse outcomes (lower extubation rates). Results Of 527 patients, 508 (96.4%) survived to discharge. Median ICU and hospital stays were 7.9 (IQR 4.8-14.8) and 13.9 (9.4-26) days, respectively. Of 523 patients with DOMV data, median DOMV was 3.9 (IQR 1.9-7.1) days ( Table 1 ) In the anatomy model, HLH had the lowest extubation rate (HR 0.3, 95% CI 0.18-0.52), followed by AVC (HR 0.44, 95% CI 0.29-0.67) and DORV-AVC (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.37-0.87). In the palliation model, stage 1 palliation (HR 0.6, 95% CI 0.43-0.85) and ventricular recruitment (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.46-0.9) had the lowest extubation rates (p<0.001). After adjustment, younger age, longer bypass time, higher VIS (all modest), and renal dysfunction were independently associated with lower extubation rates (Figure 1). In the anatomy-palliation model, Other + stage 1 had the lowest extubation rate (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.13-0.62), followed by all forms of palliated DORV-AVC and AVC (all p<0.05) (Figure 2). Conclusion BiV repair was associated with high survival to hospital discharge. Postoperative DOMV varied by anatomy and prior palliation strategy, with HLH, DORV-AVC and AVC subgroups, as well as those with prior stage 1 and ventricular recruitment palliation at highest risk for prolonged DOMV. Findings may inform perioperative counseling and resource planning.
nd0da6d20776e: Background: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for approximately half of all heart failure cases and is characterized by exercise intolerance, impaired quality of life, and high morbidity. Gene set enrichment analyses identified differentially expressed pathways associated with HFpEF and KCCQ score. Results: HFpEF patients were primarily female (64%), mean age 70 +/-12 years, 25% African American, 50% diabetes, 94% hypertension, with mean BMI 31.6 kg/m2 with controls demographically matched. ( Figure A ) As expected, HFpEF patients had worse KCCQ overall summary score (49.9 +/-19.2 vs 75.2 +/-17.6) vs controls. Brachial vein endothelial transcriptome analysis identified 1536 genes (1167 upregulated, 369 downregulated, nominal p<0.05) differentially expressed between HFpEF vs controls ( Figure B ) with hierarchical clustering between groups. ( Figure C ) The top upregulated pathways in HFpEF included mitochondrial and ribosome biogenesis, collagen formation, and cellular response to starvation. Conclusions: We describe the first study of vascular endothelial cell transcriptomics in HFpEF, identifying a distinct transcriptomic signature independently associated with impaired quality of life. These findings highlight potential mechanisms underlying endothelial dysfunction in HFpEF and their relationship to clinically meaningful outcomes.

n0683badddb57: Background: Landmark trials established carotid endarterectomy (CEA) for asymptomatic carotid stenosis decades ago, but advances in modern medical therapy (MMT) have lowered baseline stroke risk and called the incremental benefit of revascularization into question. nd0396a258a54: Randomized trials have shown limited benefits and increased risks of adding spinal fusion surgery to decompression for degenerative spondylolisthesis. Decompression with fusion has increasingly been used in the United States. To examine the comparative effectiveness of decompression with fusion versus decompression alone for patient subgroups. Cohort study using the target trial framework. Norwegian Registry for Spine Surgery and nested NORDSTEN-DS (Norwegian degenerative spondylolisthesis and spinal stenosis) randomized trial. Adults aged 18 to 80 years with lumbar degenerative spondylolisthesis and symptomatic back or leg pain lasting at least 3 months. Lumbar spinal decompression surgery with fusion versus lumbar spinal decompression surgery alone. The primary outcomes were Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) score and reoperation at 12 months. Linear regression models with inverse probability weighting to control for baseline confounding were used to obtain effect estimates with 95% CIs for decompression with fusion versus decompression alone for prespecified subgroups, including sex, age, smoking, body mass index (BMI), back pain intensity, and American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) grade. Of 2252 patients, 236 were in the NORDSTEN-DS randomized trial. The mean age was 66 years, and 1576 (70%) women were included. A total of 1446 patients had decompression alone, and 806 had decompression with fusion; respective unadjusted baseline ODI scores were 38.9 (SD, 14.9) and 41.4 (SD, 14.7). At 12 months, the ODI score was 22.3 (95% CI, 15.5 to 29.1) for decompression alone and 20.0 (CI, 13.9 to 26.2) for decompression with fusion; the mean difference was 2.2 (CI, -1.6 to 6.1). In exploratory analyses, the ODI score was worse for decompression with fusion for men with BMI of 30 kg/m2 or higher. Reoperation risk at 12 months did not differ. Possible residual confounding. Patient subgroups did not have differential effects from the addition of fusion to decompression at 12 months. Research Council of Norway.

n03e5666e9269: Long COVID (LC) is widespread; however, limited information has been reported on the likelihood that symptoms remit over time. To evaluate the likelihood of improvement among persons with likely LC. Prospective, multisite cohort study (RECOVER-Adult [Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery]). 83 U.S.-based sites across 33 states; Washington, DC; and Puerto Rico. 1019 persons in RECOVER-Adult with likely LC (LC Research Index [LCRI] ≥11) 12 months after first SARS-CoV-2 infection. The primary outcome was time until 2 consecutive study visits with LCRI less than 11. Secondary outcomes were time until LCRI measure reduced 50% or more and quality of life was good or better, and LCRI decreased to 0. Unadjusted estimates of cumulative incidence and adjusted marginal cumulative incidence by age, sex, SARS-CoV-2 wave, and LC subtype were reported across all follow-up time points. An estimated 36.2% (95% CI, 33.0% to 39.5%) met the primary outcome by 24 months after infection, and 50.1% (CI, 46.1% to 54.0%) met the primary outcome by 36 months. An estimated 56.4% (CI, 52.2% to 60.4%) and 26.9% (CI, 23.3% to 30.5%), respectively, met the 2 secondary outcomes by 36 months. Among persons who still reported likely LC at 18 months and 24 months after first infection, relative timing of subsequent symptom improvement was similar. Findings in this observational cohort are interpretable in a population with prevalent likely LC and do not address causal relationships between individual characteristics and symptom improvement. Among persons with likely LC 12 months after initial SARS-CoV-2 infection, one half experience meaningful reductions in symptoms by 36 months, whereas a quarter experience complete remission of symptoms. These findings underscore both the potential for natural recovery and the urgent need for placebo-controlled therapeutic intervention trials. National Institutes of Health.

n36711ffe3a9c: One critical shortcoming of many clinical therapeutic trials is their focus on short-term effects, leaving unanswered questions about how participants fare in the longer term. Trial extension studies are conducted to address this gap, allowing assessment of both durability of treatment benefit (eg, whether disease remission or improvements in function are maintained or diminished over time) and long-term safety (such as incidence of delayed adverse events). In therapeutic trials, extension studies can mitigate the ethical burden associated with discontinuation of potentially effective treatments or long-term administration of placebo or inferior interventions among those initially assigned to the control group. The prospect of an extension study may also give participants greater incentive to enroll in trials, despite concerns about being assigned to the control group in the initial phase of the research. Because extension studies build on existing trial infrastructure, they also allow additional and potentially valuable information to be derived from trials that already require significant up-front investment.

n301b4b9cd03d: If medicine too readily imagines the body as machine, the poem “Eternal life” proposes poetry itself as a deeper, more marvelously humane technology. Against a searchable database and a website’s archived obituary photographs, the poem offers its own elegant processing, synthesis, and preservation, which do not merely confirm whether someone has died, but restore the departed in the small gestures that make each one memorably human. Thus an implicit comparison emerges, with medicine’s view of decline and mortality as mechanical failure and retrievable data points contrasted with poetry’s returning of meaning, not a device for defeating or quantifying death, but a form for giving the deceased back to consciousness. The phone downloads a photograph and the website records a name as seamlessly as physicians might imagine how the brain stores and recalls memories. Yet neither can revivify the people the speaker’s father once knew, as it takes poetry to deliver the sweet sharing of sugar and the click of a returned key unlocking a door. The familiar medical fantasy of cybernetic immortality through synchronicity conquering biological decay is replaced by the strange kindness of poetry’s perfectly imperfect recollection, with loved ones absent at one moment but then lucidly present again the next. Forgetting, medically construed as neurological malfunction, becomes instead a porous border across which the dead may return through poetry’s dream-making. Poetry ultimately offers its own godlike machinery: “A last untouched memory/That kept giving them back to you/Eternally” concludes the poem, as if granting the eternal life announced in its title.

n9e1955af9b2e: Prescription drug manufacturers typically apply to the US Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) for patents to protect their products from generic competition. The primary patent on a drug covers the core active ingredient and generally lasts 20 years. Because these patents are often granted early in drug development, however, the effective period of patent protection after US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval is usually 7 to 12 years. Once that period ends, generic versions may enter the market and compete with the brand-name drug, often leading to a rapid and substantial decline in price. The statutory framework for drug patents is established in the Hatch-Waxman Act of 1984. In addition to patent protection, brand-name drugs may qualify for periods of exclusivity granted by the FDA, which may run concurrently with patents or separately.

ne9e8bae073bb: Cancer is a growing health and economic burden worldwide, yet comprehensive global estimates of cancer treatment costs are sparse. Such data are crucial for economic evaluations to inform policy making and practice to improve cancer control and outcomes. We aimed to synthesise available estimates of direct cancer treatment costs by stage, year, and follow-up period and predict global cancer treatment costs. In this systematic review and modelling study, we extracted estimates of cancer treatment costs (ie, direct treatment costs only) from the medical literature, screening 25 896 studies, of which 196 were included in our final dataset, covering 31 cancer types across 44 countries. Costs were standardised as a ratio of country GDP per capita and adjusted for follow-up period. We used a Bayesian hierarchical model to synthesise the estimates as a function of GDP per capita, accounting for cancer type, stage (I-IV), year of diagnosis, and follow-up period. We then estimated global and regional treatment costs (overall and by cancer type) in US$ 2022 based on the latest available incidence data from GLOBOCAN. This study is registered on PROSPERO (#CRD420251138446). Globally, total 10-year treatment costs for newly diagnosed cancers in 2022 were estimated to be $771·48 billion (95% UI 719·99-823·81), with breast cancer being the largest driver of costs ($96·07 billion [80·78-109·43]), followed by leukaemia ($86·11 billion [80·36-94·87]) and lung cancer ($84·36 billion [73·18-95·28]). North America and Europe accounted for 64% of total costs, but only 36% of diagnosed cancer cases. Mean costs per diagnosed patient were $38 650 (95% UI 36 070-41 280) globally, ranging from $3380 (95% UI 2960-3820) in eastern Africa to $93 600 (95% UI 87 170-100 150) in North America. nc0f16d18b824: BackgroundVEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are considered the backbone for the treatment of metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. n939d3be5d6f9: BackgroundRandomized clinical trials (RCTs) have compared laparoscopic liver resection (LLR) and open liver resection (OLR) for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM); however, long-term outcomes and subgroup effects have not been comprehensively evaluated.PurposeTo compare postoperative and long-term oncologic outcomes after LLR versus OLR for CRLM using individual participant data from RCTs.Data sourcesPubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from database inception through March 2025 for RCTs comparing LLR and OLR for CRLM.Study selectionEligible studies were RCTs comparing LLR and OLR for CRLM.Data extractionIndividual participant data, including unpublished data, were obtained from trial investigators of all 4 published RCTs.Data synthesisAnalyses used a modified intention-to-treat approach and 1-stage individual participant data meta-analysis (IPDMA) with trial-adjusted regression models and g-computation to estimate standardized treatment effects across outcomes, with 95% CIs obtained by nonparametric bootstrap resampling. n614e43669602: To the Editor The Viewpoint article by Drs Singh and Mello provides a balanced discussion of advertising in artificial intelligence (AI)–powered clinical decision support (CDS). It is worth highlighting that the authors state that AI-powered CDS often is free. Did we not say the same about drug company–sponsored lunches and so-called “free” pens and other giveaways in the 1990s? Some will recall when drug companies sponsored lunches for faculty and trainees, gave away pens and other branded items, and sometimes accompanied physicians on rounds. For those who trained more recently, please know that this practice was widely accepted; however, we eventually learned that there is, in fact, no free lunch. Now, we must learn there is no free CDS. Singh and Mello note that while “some products operate on a subscription model, others such as OpenEvidence use advertising revenue to offer access without charge.” It is surprising and disappointing that clinicians may think they are receiving CDS for free. Perhaps they have forgotten—or may have never learned—that drug company advertisements influence prescribing behavior when they appear alongside information intended to educate physicians and support clinical practice. Clearly the drug companies themselves have not forgotten. Twenty years ago, the International Federation of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers and Associations revised its code of ethics and barred gifts or money that could influence prescribing behavior. CDS companies that embed pharmaceutical advertisements in their products should end this practice and, if they do not, the pharmaceutical industry should do so. Better yet, clinicians should recognize they have other options without industry advertisements and should choose such CDS tools.
ndd27c90df34d: In Reply We appreciate the thoughtful letters in response to our Viewpoint. We agree with Dr Ziegelstein that the simplest solution to the ethical quandaries of advertising in AI-powered CDS tools would be for the AI-powered CDS companies that use advertisements and/or the pharmaceutical companies that partner with them to end this practice altogether. However, this is unlikely to happen, given that advertising is a potentially more lucrative revenue source than other options such as subscriptions. Ziegelstein’s suggestion that clinicians recognize they have other options and choose CDS tools that do not embed advertisements seems more realistic, particularly if their organizational employers nudge them in this direction. Historically, once Epocrates (a free drug information app) began supporting ads at the point of care, its credibility with its physician users eroded and other services such as UpToDate ultimately won out.

n1bce3d09872e: “Do I need to treat this blood pressure?” is one of the most common questions to pass through the minds of acute care pediatricians during a typical day in the hospital. Blood pressure generally increases with somatic growth, reflecting developmental changes in stroke volume, vascular structure and function, and neurohumoral regulation. As a result of interindividual variation across the developmental stages of childhood, there is a wide range of acceptable blood pressure values. There is also long-standing ambiguity about what should be considered the limits of acceptable blood pressure, particularly among hospitalized children. Age-based reference values offer a starting point, although the threshold used to identify an unusually low blood pressure may differ from the pressure needed to maintain adequate organ perfusion. This uncertainty can create substantial tension when a clinician faces the decision whether to manage potentially low blood pressure in a child. Treatments for potentially low blood pressure can also vary widely, from temporary stimulation to administration of vasopressor and inotropic medications through a central vascular catheter. The clinical question of whether to manage low blood pressure is driven by concern that withholding treatment could cause harm that is hard to measure.
n0a8e551601ba: Although international guidelines recommend intrauterine insemination (IUI) with ovarian stimulation as first-line treatment for unexplained infertility, evidence from comparisons of this method with in vitro fertilization (IVF) is limited. nbd649d566418: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is the most common form of kidney cancer, with 435 000 patients newly diagnosed worldwide each year. n1d78a20a6861: The treatment landscape of EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer harbouring exon 19 deletion or L858R mutations has advanced remarkably over the past two decades. nbf23cba0be20: BackgroundNational cancer control plans (NCCPs) vary in scope and comprehensiveness, yet expert-led review is resource intensive and limits cross-country comparability. neb745a437649: Patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma were historically deemed incurable and treated with palliative intent. n9b8e8ddc7353: Up to 12% of childhood cancer survivors have an underlying cancer predisposition syndrome (CPS). n499627ac072d: BackgroundAnti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy is the standard second-line treatment for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. ne805cbc8e893: BackgroundDivarasib, a next-generation, oral KRAS G12C inhibitor, is more potent and selective in vitro than the first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib.MethodsIn this phase 3, international, open-label trial, patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomly assigned to receive divarasib orally at a dose of 400 mg once daily or control treatment (sotorasib orally at a dose of 960 mg once daily or adagrasib orally at a dose of 600 mg twice daily) until the occurrence of disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, loss of clinical benefit, withdrawal of consent, death, or trial termination. nc84ddc78d69c: BackgroundSavolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). naabad6018a64: Offering late-line systemic therapy to patients with chemo-refractory metastatic colorectal cancer demands a careful estimation of the balance between the expected treatment benefit and its potential impact on quality of life, including adverse events, hospital visits, and psychosocial consequences.1 In such a comprehensive and individualised assessment of patients’ general conditions, usually summarised by Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status, the cumulative burden of disease-related symptoms and previous treatment-related adverse events, together with the potential decay of organ functional reserve, cannot be neglected.

neade2a36331e: Large-scale genome-wide association studies have identified hundreds of multiple sclerosis risk loci, most of which implicate immune pathways and establish multiple sclerosis as a highly polygenic, immune-mediated disease. n388921f77d7b: The Victorian painter Richard Dadd was born in 1817. By the time of his death in 1886 he had been detained in psychiatric hospitals for 42 years. nc323dcc0f863: The discovery of antibody-mediated glial and neuronal disorders has transformed the diagnosis and treatment of neurological diseases previously considered idiopathic or not recognised as immune-mediated. The broad, heterogeneous presentations of autoimmune encephalitides require coordinated multidisciplinary care within and beyond neurology, involving specialists in paediatrics, infectious diseases, epilepsy, movement disorders, sleep medicine, intensive care, cognitive rehabilitation, and other relevant disciplines. Such interdisciplinary collaboration facilitates the recognition of new diseases and elucidation of the causes of previously unclassified disorders. Improving patient care requires not only aetiological and mechanistic insight to enable development of targeted therapies but also strengthened cross-specialty expertise to optimise diagnosis and management.
n5729197f38e9: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) affect more than 220 million people worldwide and are associated with cardiometabolic, endocrine, neurological, and psychiatric sequelae for years to decades after an acute injury. n610f679f14c5: Health professionals and policy makers should fully support the students currently protesting in France.1 Apart from the regrettable outbursts of violence happening during protests, this movement reflects the anger of youth at decades of successive policies, both at national and global levels, which have progressively widened educational inequalities. n1d8ac6a16ca9: Degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM), the most common non-traumatic spinal cord injury, is a prevalent, progressive, and highly disabling neurological disease, causing heterogeneous impairment ranging from sensory loss and impaired hand dexterity to gait, balance, and autonomic dysfunction. Disability often persists despite surgical decompression, and untreated disease can progress to irreversible neurological injury, including tetraplegia. Current clinical management is largely reactive, with diagnosis and intervention typically only after neurological deterioration has become clinically apparent and radiographic evidence of cervical myelopathy is established. Advances in multimodal diagnostics over the past 5 years are now enabling the detection of subtle spinal cord injury, biological disease activity, and subclinical neurodegeneration before overt clinical disability. Quantitative spinal cord MRI, advanced neurophysiological assessments, dynamic biomechanical metrics, and sensitive functional testing provide complementary tools for early detection, risk stratification, and prognostication. Together, these approaches are redefining DCM as a disease that should be managed proactively. Evidence supports decompressive surgery in patients with moderate-to-severe disease, whereas in milder disease or in spinal stenosis that might develop into DCM, the management of patients should be interdisciplinary, with active surveillance to detect early deterioration or decompressive surgery in selected cases. Improved prediction of disease trajectories and clearer evidence on long-term outcomes could enable selective earlier intervention and help to prevent neurological disability.
n2adff0cef0e3: The UK (chiefly driven by England and Scotland) is expected to be the first country to meet WHO's goal for the elimination of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection by 2030. n22a7e8b53682: In many disease settings, physicians and patients can choose between several treatment options that are in common use, but how should they make the choice? n94a9e0fcb5d2: Much health advocacy is driven by single-issue activism. Communities with a common interest—from AIDS to child health, climate to tobacco control—focus intensely on their own domain. nb8510b0ee181: By 2050, almost 1 billion people are expected to live with osteoarthritis—a disabling musculoskeletal condition with currently no cure. n3c52f9a5e96d: Our decisions today can support or threaten future human health. n9ace97f52042: This report from the Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health lays out a foresight-driven, health-focused approach to identifying and prioritising major threats to global health over the remainder of the century. We argue that recent global shocks (including COVID-19, Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease, major geopolitical conflict, accelerating climate impacts, rapid shifts in development assistance, and the emergence of powerful artificial intelligence [AI] systems) show how quickly assumptions about stability can be overturned—and why governments and multilateral institutions must counter short-termism and localism with systematic, repeatable risk assessment and preparedness planning.
n3236834c743b: BackgroundDespite high invasive breast cancer detection rates, the effectiveness of digital breast tomosynthesis screening is still uncertain. The cumulative incidence of invasive interval cancers at 12 months in screen-negative women was the prespecified secondary outcome.
